subject: Pilot environment preflight & action plan: MedScale POC
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Simmons <j.simmons@medscale.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot environment preflight & action plan: MedScale POC

Hi Jordan — great to connect last week. Per our demo and the evaluation objectives you shared, I pulled together a short preflight checklist and proposed cadence so your engineering team can get the POC environment ready with minimum friction. Attached is a one-page MAP draft and a network template you can hand to ops.

Key items we need to lock down this week so the pilot can start the week of Apr 5:
- Org & service account: invite a MedScale service account (sa-medscale@medscale.io) to the Redwood evaluation org (role: inference-runner).
- API keys: we need one short-lived API key for testing and one long-lived read-only key for metrics ingestion.
- IP allowlist: provide CIDR ranges that should be whitelisted (we call these app-to-platform egresss).
- VPC peering window: propose Apr 1–2 for peering/final network validation (2–4 hour maintenance window).

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Mar 19: agree MAP milestones and network contacts (this thread)
- Mar 22: MedScale creates service account + shares IP ranges; Redwood creates initial API keys
- Apr 1–2: VPC peering and smoke tests
- Apr 5: pilot acceptance (first 100k tokens, basic eval prompts)

Can you confirm who on your side owns network provisioning so we can calendar the peering window? Also attaching the MAP draft and a network-config template to speed handoff.

Attachments: [Attachment: MedScale_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (application/pdf)], [Attachment: network-config-template.yaml (text/yaml)]

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once we have a peering contact.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot environment preflight & action plan: MedScale POC

Hi Diego — thanks for the clear plan and the MAP draft. Asha (VP Eng) will own network provisioning, I’m looping her in. A few quick items from our side:
- Can you confirm what data is logged to Redwood tracing for the pilot (we need to validate PII handling before creating service accounts)?
- We’ll need a SOC 2 artifact (or link to the attestation) before we grant network peering.
- The earliest our infra can do peering is Apr 2 in the 10:00–14:00 PT window.

We’ll go ahead and create a service account (sa-medscale@medscale.io) and share the exact CIDRs by EOD Tue Mar 23. Will that timeline work for you?

— Jordan
Jordan Simmons
Director of Product, MedScale

Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot environment preflight & action plan: MedScale POC

Jordan / Asha — Karthik here (infra). Quick answers and next steps from a network/ops perspective:
- Logging/PII: for the pilot we only capture request metadata, token counts and anonymized latency metrics by default. No user text is forwarded to external analytics. If you want stricter redaction we can enable text-stripping on the ingestion path (adds ~20ms latency).
- SOC2: attaching a pointer below — we can share the attestation PDF via your secure S3 link or a signed DocuSign delivery.
- Peering details: Apr 2, 10:00–14:00 PT works. We suggest a 2-hour window starting at 10:30 PT to run peering + smoke tests. Requirements for your infra:
  * Provide two CIDR blocks for the peering (primary + management)
  * Confirm route priorities and whether you plan to NAT egress to internet from your side (if yes, we’ll tighten exit filters)
  * Ensure the service account has the following: compute.networkUser, iam.serviceAccountUser (we only read project metadata).

I’m attaching a minimal network-config-template.yaml that contains the peering acceptance criteria and sample BGP values. Please paste the completed yaml back into the thread so we can validate automatically on our side.

Thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps and owners so we have a single source of truth:
1) Mar 23 (MedScale) — share completed network-config-template.yaml with CIDRs and peering BGP values (owner: Asha)
2) Mar 24 (Redwood) — Redwood publishes a short SOC2 pointer and creates the initial API keys (owner: Marissa) -> keys: test-XXXXXXXX (short-lived), ingest-YYYYYYYY (read-only)
3) Apr 2 10:30–12:30 PT — VPC peering & smoke tests (owner: Karthik / MedScale infra)
4) Apr 5 — Pilot acceptance: smoke test results + first 100k tokens (owner: Diego / Jordan)

I’ve uploaded the MAP draft and network template to the shared Drive (link below) and attached a PDF for your security team. Please confirm by EOD tomorrow so Marissa can spin keys and we can calendar the peering slot.

Attachments: [Attachment: MedScale_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (application/pdf)], [Attachment: network-config-template.yaml (text/yaml)]
